    R0.8 · Playable research prototype · Fictional institutions · Shared-screen play, not network multiplayer · Progress saves on this browser. Original KFB die
    A SHORT MEETING. LASTING OBLIGATIONS.

    Take a seat.

    Build a three-institution network. Make useful connections. Borrow someone else’s.

    Eight rounds. Bank your network points after each turn. One action. No elimination. Narration optional. All six seats use the same rules.

    The business of being indispensable.

    Goal: earn the most secured points over eight turns. After your completed turn, bank 1 per active institution and 2 more per satisfied need. Banked points cannot be stolen. At the end, add your role’s 2-point bonus once if fulfilled. Multiplayer: Favor breaks equal scores; equal Favor means a shared win. Solo: equal scores are a System win, regardless of Favor.

    Each turn: gain 1 Favor, up to 3. RECRUIT from the market, POACH an exposed rival, or play your single Plot. Your network holds at most three institutions; choose one to return if full.

    Recruit: costs 0 inside the window or in the unique dominant dice channel, otherwise 1. Tied highest dice has no free channel. Costs also apply to fallback and Bailout; Bailout refunds 1 afterwards.

    Poach: costs 1. Target a rival card with an unmet need, or any card in a full network. Only its owner responds: spend 2 Favor to VETO or allow the transfer. A veto gives the attacker an affordable recruit fallback. No affordable card? The turn ends.

    Plots: Audit suspends one card; Broker attempts a free poach; Bailout recruits then gains 1 Favor; Frame turns a die ±1 or swaps two dice, then recruits. In window mode it shifts the frame one slot. Discard a useless Plot to draw another, as your whole action.

    Public Hearing: each full network automatically suspends its least damaging card for this round. Suspended cards supply nothing and produce zero points when your turn is scored. Previously banked points stay yours. Funding gives smaller networks 1 Favor. The final event is always Funding; an Audit can affect production on a later turn; it never removes banked points.

    Solo: the System starts with one institution, has no role or Plot, follows public-state choices, and can veto. It has no access to future cards. The visible computer styles are policies, not human psychology.

    3D board: each row is a supply channel and each column a market slot. Only four cards exist; empty cells are not extra cards. A focus opens its row for free recruitment. Click a card to inspect, then confirm in the action panel. Drag to orbit; scroll or use +/− to zoom; Shift-drag to pan; Reset returns to the readable home view. Everything is playable using the text controls. R/A/F labels and colors identify dice; no extra hidden dice powers. No performance or storytelling points.

    The next seat may now reveal its Plot.
